title: Preparing Your Project for Shipping 🧹
description: Clean up assets, set game defaults, and configure project settings for release.

slides.title: From Editor to Player 🚀
slides.content:
# Shipping Your Game

Before building an executable, you must prepare your project. This means cleaning up test assets, setting the right game mode, and ensuring the startup sequence works without the editor.

* **Shipping** is the final build type – optimised, no editor tools, no console.
* **Development** build is for testing with some debug features.
* **Debug** build is for deep bug hunting (not for distribution).

Your goal: a self‑contained `.exe` (Windows) or `.app` (Mac) that players can launch.

quizData.question: Which build configuration is best for the final player release?
quizData.explanation: Shipping builds are stripped of debug symbols and editor features, giving maximum performance and smaller size.

slides.title: Essential Project Settings ⚙️
slides.content:
# Set the Defaults

Open **Edit → Project Settings** and check these categories:

* **Maps & Modes** – set Game Default Map (your first level) and Default GameMode.
* **Packaging** – define the build output directory and game title.
* **Supported Platforms** – check only the platforms you intend to release on (speeds up cooking).
* **Rendering** – disable unused features (e.g., Ray Tracing if not needed).

Also ensure **Startup Movies** (if any) are set, and the **Splash Screen** looks professional.

quizData.question: The Game Default Map is the level that loads when the packaged game starts.
quizData.explanation: It defines the initial map, just like the Editor Startup Map but for standalone builds.

slides.title: Asset Cleanup 🧹
slides.content:
## Remove the Bloat

Before packaging:

* Delete unused test levels, old Blueprints, and placeholder assets.
* Use the **Reference Viewer** (right‑click an asset) to see if anything is still referenced.
* Run **File → Validate Data** to check for broken links.
* Ensure all assets have correct compression and texture sizes (no 4K textures for mobile).

A clean project cooks faster and builds a smaller package.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the Size Map

Right‑click any folder → **Size Map**. It shows a visual tree of how much disk space each asset consumes. Find and remove the heavy ones you don't need.
